hunks.baseline: The world was full of incidents and all the possibilities that followed from them.
hunks.sol: The world was full of events and the possibilities that followed them.

hunks.baseline: No matter how far civilization advanced, no matter how cutting-edge science reached into realms once beyond its grasp, there was no such thing as a perfect, one-hundred-percent certainty.
hunks.sol: No matter how far civilization advanced, no matter how deeply cutting-edge science reached into realms once beyond its grasp, there was no such thing as absolute, one-hundred-percent certainty.

hunks.baseline: And that was all the more true when it came to people, rather than machines.
hunks.sol: Especially where people, rather than machines, were concerned.

hunks.baseline: But at this very moment—
hunks.sol: But at this moment—

hunks.baseline: Looking at those trembling gray eyes, I was certain.
hunks.sol: Looking at his trembling gray eyes, I was certain.

hunks.baseline: At last, I’d driven him—Michael Silbert—to the edge of the cliff.
hunks.sol: At last, I’d driven Michael Silbert to the edge of a cliff.

hunks.baseline: But I wiped the smile from my lips.
My disgust for the man standing before me outweighed any joy at having turned the tables.
hunks.sol: But I wiped the smile from my lips. My disgust for the man before me outweighed any pleasure I took in turning the tables.

hunks.baseline: I despised everything about the man drenched in gray.
hunks.sol: I despised everything about that man steeped in gray.

hunks.baseline: My voice slipped past my lips and shattered the silence.
hunks.sol: My voice broke the silence.

hunks.baseline: And unlike when I’d revealed the Skeleton King’s identity, not one person in the room laughed at me this time.
hunks.sol: Unlike when I’d revealed the Skeleton King’s identity, not one person in the room laughed at me this time.

hunks.baseline: Or perhaps the truth was so far beyond anything they’d expected that they couldn’t bring themselves to accept it.
hunks.sol: Or perhaps they couldn’t bring themselves to accept a truth so far beyond anything they’d imagined.

hunks.baseline: It was the Guild Master of Kronos. I kept my eyes fixed on Michael Silbert as I answered.
hunks.sol: The Guild Master of Kronos. I kept my eyes on Michael Silbert as I answered.

hunks.baseline: “Ask the man himself.”
hunks.sol: “Ask him yourself.”

hunks.baseline: In the suffocating silence, hundreds of pairs of eyes turned toward Michael Silbert.
hunks.sol: In the suffocating silence, hundreds of pairs of eyes turned toward Michael Silbert. Among those watching were his supporters—some I’d identified through my investigation, and some I hadn’t.

hunks.baseline: Among them were some of his supporters who’d already known from their investigation, and others who hadn’t.
“From what I saw earlier, you were all busy kissing his ass. Guess none of you had anyone to tell you what was really going on. Well, that figures. Doesn’t it?”
hunks.sol: “You were all kissing his ass from every angle earlier. Guess nobody bothered telling you what was really going on. Well, I can see why. Can’t you?”

hunks.baseline: There were still ripples in his gray eyes, and I felt as if I could read all the thoughts that must be swirling around in his head.
hunks.sol: His gray eyes were still unsettled, and I could almost read the thoughts racing through his head.

hunks.baseline: “Don’t strain yourself trying to figure it out. You already know, don’t you?”
hunks.sol: “Don’t strain yourself thinking. You already know, don’t you?”

hunks.baseline: Once every piece of the puzzle was in place, the answer was clear.
hunks.sol: Once all the equations lined up, the answer was clear.

hunks.baseline: It felt like I’d finally escaped a maze I’d been wandering through for ages.
hunks.sol: I felt as if I’d finally found my way out of a maze I’d wandered for ages.

hunks.baseline: And beyond the walls that had hemmed me in on every side, one person waited at the exit.
hunks.sol: Beyond the walls that had hemmed me in on every side, someone waited at the exit.

hunks.baseline: A gray monster who’d lingered somewhere between light and darkness, then crossed the river from which there was no return.
hunks.sol: A gray monster who’d lingered somewhere between light and darkness, then crossed a river from which there was no return.

hunks.baseline: The last edge of the veil that had hidden his true nature—
hunks.sol: The last edge of the veil hiding what he really was.

hunks.baseline: *So intense.*

hunks.sol: His fingertips met the cold armor that covered the wound, rising all the way to his neck, and a dry laugh escaped him.

hunks.baseline: In a situation like this, they were meaningless. They would only make him look pathetic.
hunks.sol: Meaningless now. They would only make him look pathetic.

hunks.sol: As a single drop of water could split a rock, one palm-sized bottle of potion was enough to bring down the mountain that was Michael Silbert.

hunks.sol: How had Jin Taekyung learned the secret? And what had made him willing to use a double-edged sword fraught with danger and uncertainty against Michael?

hunks.baseline: So instead of making excuses, Michael Silbert chose to ask.
hunks.sol: So instead of making excuses, Michael Silbert asked.

hunks.baseline: It was a brief question directed at Jin Taekyung. But the shock it sent through the room was immense.
hunks.sol: The question was brief, but the shock it sent through the room was immense.

hunks.sol: “Yeah. Turns out the man investigated all sorts of things before he died.”

hunks.sol: A sheet of paper flew toward Michael like an arrow. He caught it between two fingers and read the title at the top.

hunks.baseline: “They say he was the greatest monster scholar of his age, even before you count his being a Grand Mage. Looks like he researched just about everything.”
hunks.sol: “They say he was the greatest monster scholar of his age, even before he was a Grand Mage. He researched just about everything.”

hunks.baseline: “Sure. That’s what people knew.”
hunks.sol: “Sure. Not that anyone knew of.”

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert silently looked down at the paper in his hand.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert looked down at the paper in his hand. His gray eyes darted across it; he read and understood the entire page in an instant.

hunks.baseline: His gray eyes moved quickly. It took him only an instant to read and understand the entire page.

“Studying the possibility of introducing a monster’s magical power into a human body and making the two coexist. That’s the kind of crazy idea only a lunatic like Siegfried Bassman could come up with. Of course…”
hunks.sol: “Studying whether a human body could take in a monster’s magical power and coexist with it. Sounds like the sort of insane idea only an eccentric like Siegfried Bassman would pursue. Of course…”

hunks.baseline: Jin Taekyung’s low voice rang in his ears.
hunks.sol: Jin Taekyung’s low voice reached his ears.

hunks.baseline: “That wouldn’t have been true for you.”
hunks.sol: “It wouldn’t sound insane to you.”

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert raised his head. The sheet, now hopelessly crumpled, caught fire in his grip.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert raised his head. The paper, now badly crumpled in his grip, caught fire.

hunks.baseline: *Fwoosh. Crumble.*
hunks.sol: *Fwoosh. Crackle.*

hunks.baseline: Ash drifted through the air. Beyond it, the eyes that had gone cold now held a reddish glow.
hunks.sol: Ash drifted through the air. Beyond it, a reddish heat entered Jin Taekyung’s cool, steady eyes.

hunks.baseline: “Looks like Siegfried Bassman was curious about the same thing. But even he never managed to prove it. Or maybe he stopped researching because he thought he’d crossed a taboo.”
hunks.sol: “Looks like Siegfried Bassman wondered about it too. But even he never managed to prove it. Or maybe he stopped because he thought he’d crossed a taboo.”

hunks.baseline: Jin Taekyung watched the ash as it drifted toward him and continued.
hunks.sol: Jin Taekyung watched the ash drift toward him and continued.

hunks.baseline: “Maybe he had his own reasons for not leaving this kind of material behind. Or maybe whoever killed him made sure it was gone. Either way, there was almost nothing left about that research. It took me quite a while to find that.”
hunks.sol: “Maybe he decided material like this shouldn’t be left behind. Or maybe whoever killed him wanted it gone. Either way, almost nothing remained of that research. It took me a while to find this.”

hunks.baseline: “You think this is why I killed him?”
hunks.sol: “You think that’s why I killed him?”

hunks.baseline: “At first, yeah.”
hunks.sol: “At first.”

hunks.baseline: “Right. But you had another reason for killing Siegfried Bassman.”
hunks.sol: “Yeah. But you killed Siegfried Bassman for another reason.”

hunks.baseline: “I won’t deny it. But I’d like to know why you think that.”
hunks.sol: “I won’t deny it. But I’d like to know why you think so.”

hunks.baseline: “It’s simple. You’re not careless enough to leave research materials like this lying around.”
hunks.sol: “Simple. You’re not careless enough to leave research material like this behind.”

hunks.baseline: After staring silently at Jin Taekyung for a moment, Michael Silbert laughed out loud.
hunks.sol: Michael Silbert stared at Jin Taekyung for a moment, then laughed aloud.

hunks.baseline: “I appreciate that. I would’ve been disappointed if even you thought I was an idiot.”
hunks.sol: “I appreciate that. I’d have been disappointed if even you took me for an idiot.”

hunks.baseline: “Don’t mention it. I just thought you were a piece of shit, not an idiot.”
hunks.sol: “Don’t thank me. I took you for a fucking bastard instead.”

hunks.baseline: “But you still haven’t given me a clear answer. This material alone wouldn’t have been nearly enough to make you suspect me.”
hunks.sol: “But you still haven’t given me a clear answer. This material alone couldn’t have been enough to make you suspect me.”

hunks.baseline: “No. It was enough.”
hunks.sol: “No, it was enough.”

hunks.baseline: “As I looked over what little research material was left, that thought suddenly crossed my mind.”
hunks.sol: “I was looking over what little research remained when the thought struck me.”

hunks.baseline: With a scornful sneer, Jin Taekyung turned his head.
hunks.sol: Jin Taekyung turned his head with a contemptuous sneer.

hunks.baseline: The truth behind the Grand Mage’s death—a mystery from beginning to end—had now been revealed. The stunned crowd stood frozen, staring at the two men.
hunks.sol: Now that the truth behind the Grand Mage’s death—long a mystery—had come to light, the stunned crowd stood frozen, watching the two men.

hunks.baseline: “What if Michael Silbert, that son of a bitch, really was already as good as half human and half demon? What if he’d already made that absurd research a reality?”
hunks.sol: “What if Michael Silbert, that fucking bastard, was already as good as half human and half demon? What if he’d made that absurd research a reality?”

hunks.baseline: Before hundreds of watching eyes and ears. On a stage someone other than him had planned meticulously from beginning to end.
hunks.sol: Before hundreds of watching eyes and listening ears, on a stage someone else had planned meticulously from beginning to end, he spoke as though he stood alone in the spotlight.

hunks.baseline: He spoke like a leading man standing alone in the spotlight.
“And then… finally, all the pieces fell into place.”
hunks.sol: “And then… every piece finally fell into place.”

hunks.baseline: That hypothesis no one else could have thought of was the last piece needed to complete this complicated puzzle.
hunks.sol: That possibility, one no one else had considered, was the last piece of the complicated puzzle.

hunks.baseline: Why Michael Silbert had realized the Skeleton King’s true identity.
hunks.sol: It explained how Michael Silbert had recognized the Skeleton King for what he was.

hunks.baseline: Why a man who’d been just one hero among hundreds during the Great Cataclysm had risen from the dragon’s tail to its head.
hunks.sol: How a man who’d been just one hero among hundreds during the Great Cataclysm had risen from the dragon’s tail to its head.

hunks.baseline: Why the Odin Guild had begun to grow around the time Cheon Taemin disappeared, and why Michael hadn’t shown his face even at Lee Jungryong’s funeral, attended by prominent figures from around the world.
hunks.sol: Why the Odin Guild’s growth had begun when Cheon Taemin disappeared, and why Michael hadn’t shown his face even at Lee Jungryong’s funeral, where prominent figures from around the world had gathered.

hunks.baseline: There was only one reason.
hunks.sol: All of it came down to one thing.

hunks.baseline: Jin Taekyung slowly turned around. Looking into the gray eyes that no longer wavered, he continued.
hunks.sol: Jin Taekyung slowly turned back. He looked into Michael’s gray eyes, which no longer wavered.

hunks.baseline: “I don’t know how you did it or what gave you the chance, but… you were able to grow stronger by absorbing magical power. Just like a monster.”
hunks.sol: “I don’t know how it happened or what gave you the chance, but… you were able to grow stronger by absorbing magical power. Just like a monster.”

hunks.sol: Whenever they spoke of Michael Silbert, the Skeleton King habitually called him an “unpleasant human.” Even he, a monster, couldn’t quite say what he meant by it.

hunks.baseline: If there was anyone in the world Michael Silbert feared more than anyone else, anyone whose eyes he had to avoid at all costs, it was just one person.
hunks.sol: If there was one person in the world Michael Silbert feared above all others, one person from whom he had to hide his true nature, it was—

hunks.baseline: And at the moment Jin Taekyung’s low voice reached everyone’s ears, someone’s dry lips parted, breaking the long silence.
hunks.sol: As Jin Taekyung’s low voice reached everyone in the room, a pair of dry lips parted, breaking the long silence.

hunks.baseline: “That’s why I had to live in hiding for so long. For nearly as long as you’ve been alive.”
hunks.sol: “Yes. Because of him, I had to keep my head down for many years. Almost as many as you’ve been alive.”

hunks.baseline: It had been not long after he’d gained his new power.

hunks.sol: He had only recently gained his new power. Amid a great gathering of people, that supreme being’s gaze had fixed precisely on him. Fear had gripped his entire body.

hunks.baseline: That unprecedented, turbulent power in which light and darkness had mingled for years—but which, from a certain day onward, had been stained a deeper and deeper shade by the swelling darkness.
hunks.sol: Light and darkness had mingled in it for years. Then, one day, the darkness had begun to swell, staining that strange, turbulent energy ever deeper.
